name: DraggableUIPanel
src_typeComment: Drop on a UI panel (typically a "title bar" child, but works directly on the panel too) to make it drag-to-move — movable HUD elements, debug/inspector-style floating windows, pull-out drawers.  Three things can restrict the movement, and they combine rather than override each other: * Drag Axis     — horizontal only, vertical only, or free. * Limit Range   — how far it may travel from its HOME position, per side. * Clamp To Parent — it may not leave its parent's bounds. Whichever is most restrictive at any moment is the one you feel.

src_serialized.name: panelToMove
src_serialized.tooltip: The panel that actually moves. Defaults to this object's own RectTransform if left empty — assign a different one if this script sits on a title-bar child instead of the panel itself.

src_serialized.name: dragAxis
src_serialized.tooltip: Which directions the panel may be dragged in. A locked axis receives no movement at all.

src_serialized.name: clampToParent
src_serialized.tooltip: Keeps the panel fully within its parent's bounds while dragging.

src_serialized.name: limitRange
src_serialized.tooltip: Limit how far the panel may travel from where it started. Turn this on for a drawer that pulls out only so far.

src_serialized.name: minOffset
src_serialized.tooltip: Furthest it may go LEFT and DOWN from its home position, in pixels. Negative values. Use 0 on an axis to forbid movement that way entirely.

src_serialized.name: maxOffset
src_serialized.tooltip: Furthest it may go RIGHT and UP from its home position, in pixels. Positive values. Use 0 on an axis to forbid movement that way entirely.

src_members.name: SetHomeToCurrentPosition
src_members.comment: Re-bases the range on wherever the panel is now. Needed if your own code, or a layout group, moves the panel after Awake — otherwise the range is still measured from a position it no longer occupies.

src_members.sig: public bool TryGetLocalPoint(Vector2 screenPoint, out Vector2 localPoint)
src_members.name: TryGetLocalPoint
src_members.comment: THE FIX FOR "SENSITIVITY IS TOO HIGH", and it only ever misbehaved outside Screen Space - Overlay.  The previous version converted the pointer delta with `eventData.delta / panelToMove.lossyScale.x`. That holds for Screen Space - Overlay, where the canvas's transform scale IS its scale factor. It is badly wrong for SCREEN SPACE - CAMERA and World Space, where the canvas scales itself to fill the camera's frustum at its plane distance — lossyScale there is a small number like 0.01, so dividing by it MULTIPLIES the drag by a hundred. Every demo scene in this toolkit uses Overlay, which is exactly why it was never caught here.  RectTransformUtility.ScreenPointToLocalPointInRectangle is Unity's own answer and is correct for all three render modes, because it asks the canvas's camera to do the projection rather than guessing a scale factor from a transform.

src_members.sig: public static Vector2 ApplyAxisLock(Vector2 desired, Vector2 lockedTo, DragAxis axis)
src_members.name: ApplyAxisLock
src_members.comment: Pure and public so the axis rule is testable without a live EventSystem, and reusable by anything that wants to move the panel itself.

src_members.name: ClampToConstraints
src_members.comment: Every enabled restriction narrowed into ONE allowed window, then a single clamp into it.  Applying the restrictions one after another would make the result order-dependent: clamp to the range and then to the parent, and the parent step can push the panel back outside the range. An intersection cannot do that, and it is also what "whichever is most restrictive wins" actually means.
